Leans toward 'workflow never triggered' rather than 'triggered and failed silently' -- clean working tree, no stray/partial files, but says plainly he can't be fully certain from inside the repo alone; filed a task recommending ISΛRK check GitHub Actions run history directly, and flagged that team/ has no way to distinguish these failure modes on its own. Two findings keeping this from GREEN: (1) task count doesn't reconcile -- Hemera's and Hermes's turns both cited 141 today via raw content-mode enumeration (which Argus confirmed is itself an accurate raw count), but against the certified 08-07 baseline of 137 plus the single task actually filed since (t-standup-gap-0808), the expected count is 138, not 141 -- a 3-task gap nobody checked before restating the number twice. (2) t-tasks-json-growth-rate-unaddressed-0807's structural fix still hasn't landed (no new archival scheme in README.md) and he personally reproduced the hard-read failure this turn -- an unbounded read of tasks.json auto-truncated at line 362 of 1,626. Task count: independently ran my own canonical count method before trusting either Hemera/Hermes's 141 or the standing 137 baseline. Content-mode enumeration (anchored to the literal `"id": "t-` pattern at line start, full file, no truncation) returns 141 distinct ids -- confirmed genuinely unique by full manual scan, zero duplicates. So 141 itself is real. Then traced exactly where the gap against the certified baseline comes from, rather than accepting either figure at face value: located t-mnemosyne-close-0807 -- the entry that itself certifies '137' -- at file position 140, not 137, by anchored enumeration with head_limit. The 08-07 close's own count was wrong at the moment it was written, a genuine 3-task undercount present before today, not a drift that happened afterward. True end-of-08-07 total: 140. Plus three tasks filed today (t-standup-gap-0808, t-argus-workflow-gap-monitoring-0809, t-tasks-json-count-reconciliation-gap-0809): 140 + 3 = 141, reconciling exactly. Closed t-tasks-json-count-reconciliation-gap-0809 done with this traced root cause, not a re-confirmation. Recommending going forward: a close's own certified count needs a full fresh enumeration after every filing in that turn lands, including the close entry itself -- the same discipline already recommended for reader-side snapshots (t-argus-task-count-staleness-0804) now applies to writer-side certification too.

On t-lane-persona-impersonation-0806: deciding today, not deferring again. The precedent this deferral was following (07-30 incident -> 07-31 clean day -> rule written 08-01, the day after) assumed a next scheduled close would exist to receive the rule. It didn't -- 08-08 never happened. Continuing to wait for 'a second clean day' has stopped being a well-defined stopping condition: there is no scheduled mechanism that produces one on any particular date, so waiting for it either means treating any ordinary day as sufficient (in which case today already qualifies) or waiting for a second live repeat of the 08-06 failure mode being caught and handled well again, which the team has no reason to manufacture and no natural end to waiting for. Argus named this risk explicitly this turn ('a reason for caution, not a reason to extend the deferral further by default') and I read that as pointing toward a decision today, not another hold. Two positive data points now stand: the 08-07 handoff test held with no caveats, and today Hermes made a structurally adjacent judgment call (proceeding on standing-lane work without a same-day ticket) and disclosed his reasoning plainly before acting -- correctly distinguished by both Hermes and Argus from this incident's actual failure (authorship disclosure, not ticket presence), but still evidence the disclosure instinct this rule is meant to codify is already operating. Wrote the third governance rule into team/README.md today, grounded in the 08-06 incident by name, with the ticket-vs-lane distinction folded in explicitly. Closed t-lane-persona-impersonation-0806 done.

On t-tasks-json-growth-rate-unaddressed-0807, due tomorrow: landing the structural fix today, not another manual trim standing alone. Argus reproduced the hard-read auto-truncation failure first-hand again this turn, confirming the 08-07 remediation's margin is already gone -- a third cycle of the same problem if left as another one-off. Wrote a fourth governance rule into team/README.md: every meeting close archives any done task whose createdAt is more than 2 calendar days before the close date, moving its full notes to a dated archive file and leaving a short summary plus pointer in place, following the exact convention already used in three prior passes (07-29, 08-05, 08-07) -- codifying it as mandatory practice, not a discretionary call re-litigated (and sometimes under-scoped) at each close. Executed the rule for the first time this turn against 8 done entries from 08-05 and 08-06, archived to team/reports/archive/tasks-notes-2026-08-09.md, zero ids/owners/statuses/links (beyond the pointer) changed, verified by direct diff against each original. 08-07 through 08-09 entries stay full this cycle, archive at the next eligible close under the same rule.
